question: Should Crabline always fail closed when an existing artifact directory belongs to another POSIX UID, or support a narrowly guarded recovery path for legitimate runtime-UID changes?
rationale: Strict rejection strengthens ownership guarantees but can make existing deployments unavailable after an operator or container identity change; the intended security-versus-upgrade policy cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Add guarded recovery
options.body: Preserve strict validation but provide a narrowly scoped migration or diagnostic repair flow with hostile-ownership and legitimate-upgrade coverage.

options.title: Accept fail-closed upgrades
options.body: Retain unconditional rejection and clearly document the ownership repair operators must perform before running the upgraded version.

options.title: Defer ownership enforcement
options.body: Land the independent durability fixes while postponing strict ownership enforcement until its upgrade contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Add guarded recovery
recommendation.body: Preserve strict validation but provide a narrowly scoped migration or diagnostic repair flow with hostile-ownership and legitimate-upgrade coverage.
